sources.title: Children displaced in a changing climate: Preventing and minimizing risk of displacement and preparing for climate mobility in Eastern and Southern Africa
sources.organization: UNICEF, in partnership with the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical displacement estimates for 2017–2023 and Ethiopia protection-system analysis published in September 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF–IDMC combine recorded 2017–2023 disaster displacements with georeferenced child-population proxies.
sources.limitations: Counts are conservative displacement events, not unique children; Ethiopia-specific climate-conflict and long-term outcome research is limited.

sources.title: Nothing to put in your mouth: Seeking durable solutions to drought displacement in Ethiopia
sources.temporal_coverage: Fieldwork in Somali Region in July 2019; includes displacement associated with the 2015–2017 drought and 2019 conditions.
sources.methodology: 219 purposive interviews and qualitative fieldwork in Doolo camps in July 2019.
sources.limitations: Camp sample is not representative; forced displacement is hard to distinguish from adaptive migration, and estimates omit some people remaining in place.

sources.title: The Dynamics of (Agro) Pastoral Conflicts in Eastern Ethiopia
sources.organization: Ethiopian Journal of the Social Sciences and Humanities, Addis Ababa University
geographic_coverage: Meiso-Mullu district, Shinile Zone, Somali Region
Meiso district, West Hararghe Zone, Oromia Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Fieldwork from February 2013 to November 2014; published in Volume 11, Number 1, June 2015.
sources.methodology: Mixed qualitative and quantitative study with a 128-household survey, interviews, focus groups and observations in three selected districts.
sources.limitations: Kebeles were selected for drought and conflict severity; findings reflect a small, purposively located study and respondents’ perceptions, not causal estimates.

sources.title: Ethiopia, Endline Evaluation of Satellite Index Insurance for Pastoralists (SIIPE)
sources.organization: World Food Programme Ethiopia Country Office
geographic_coverage: 11 woredas (names not given on the accessible page)
sources.temporal_coverage: SIIPE programme period 2019–2022; programme reach and evaluation findings summarized by WFP in November 2024.
sources.methodology: WFP describes a decentralized mixed-method evaluation combining quasi-experimental quantitative analysis with qualitative interviews and data.
sources.limitations: Only WFP’s evaluation landing-page summary was accessible; it gives limited estimation detail and reports missing gender-disaggregated data.

claims.paraphrase: UNICEF–IDMC estimate 1.6 million weather-related child-displacement events in Ethiopia in 2017–2023; 522,000 were drought-linked, peaking at 324,000 in 2022.

claims.locator: PDF p. 24, Ethiopia country analysis and data summary
claims.paraphrase: June–September Awash floods affect low-lying Afar and Somali communities, damaging farms, homes, schools and health facilities; drought displacement is severe in conflict-affected Somali and Oromia.
claims.limitations: This regional synthesis does not quantify climate and conflict contributions.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF says conflict in Somali and Oromia heightens drought-displacement risks.

claims.locator: PDF p. 12, displacement, conflict and insecurity; pp. 24–25, Ethiopia analysis
claims.paraphrase: Conflict-disrupted livelihoods, education and health leave children more exposed to drought/floods and at greater risk of recruitment and GBV.
claims.limitations: Synthesis, not a locality-level causal estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF links conflict-related system disruption to higher climate exposure and protection risk.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 5–7, summary, displacement context and methodology
claims.paraphrase: IDMC reported nearly 56,000 drought-affected households still displaced in Somali Region; 36,000 people were displaced in a drought context nationally in January–June 2019, mainly there.
institutions: Somali Region Disaster Prevention and Preparedness Bureau
claims.limitations: Historical estimates; drought, adaptive migration, poverty and forced displacement are difficult to distinguish.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 8–10, drought effects and pastoralist vulnerability in Doolo Zone
claims.paraphrase: In Gafow and Koracle, key informants estimated households lost up to 80% of livestock in the 2015–2017 drought; herds and milk fell as families sought clean water and aid in peri-urban Warder.
claims.limitations: Livestock-loss figure is a key-informant estimate, not a regional census.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 5–6 and 9–10, humanitarian response and conditions in Doolo and Warder
claims.paraphrase: IDMC found Doolo drought-displaced households faced food insecurity and poor water access, while aid shrank as intercommunal conflicts took priority; host communities also lacked services.
claims.limitations: Findings describe the 2019 context, not current aid levels.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: IDMC says intercommunal conflict took priority as Somali Region humanitarian aid shrank.

claims.locator: Journal pp. 39–42, methods and ranked factors encouraging rival communities to instigate conflict
claims.paraphrase: In the 128-household study across Meiso-Mullu, Meiso and Amibara, respondents ranked recurrent drought first among conflict-instigating factors because it reduced water, pasture and crop availability.
geographies: Meiso-Mullu district, Shinile Zone, Somali Region
Meiso district, West Hararghe Zone, Oromia Region
claims.limitations: Kebeles were purposively selected for drought and conflict severity; rankings are perceptions, not causal estimates.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Authors report drought as a top perceived trigger through effects on water, grazing and crops, alongside political and resource factors.

claims.locator: Journal pp. 30–35 and 47–48, institutional and political dimensions of resource conflict
claims.paraphrase: The study describes weak customary institutions, contested regional boundaries and selected officials’ interests as factors shaping resource violence; federal military interventions were often temporary rather than lasting solutions.
claims.limitations: The article reports a small historical study and does not assess subsequent institutional changes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Authors link weak customary resolution and temporary interventions to recurrent resource-based pastoral conflict.

claims.locator: WFP evaluation page, programme description and reach summary
claims.paraphrase: WFP reports that SIIPE expanded from three to 11 Somali Region woredas and reached over 28,000 households by 2021 through subsidized drought livestock insurance, public works and financial-literacy training.
geographies: 11 woredas (not named on the accessible page)
claims.limitations: Reach and programme design are WFP-reported; the accessible page does not name the participating woredas.

claims.locator: WFP evaluation page, impact findings and conclusions
claims.paraphrase: WFP’s summarized evaluation found improved insurance knowledge, financial-service engagement, livestock spending on water, veterinary care and forage, and food security, but no gains in incomes, assets or dietary diversity.
claims.limitations: These mixed evaluation findings are taken from WFP’s summary page; full estimation details were not accessible.

claims.locator: WFP evaluation page, effectiveness, scale and sustainability findings
claims.paraphrase: WFP reports complex enrolment, delayed or inadequate payouts, unreliable satellite data, low awareness, capacity gaps, unaffordable premiums and budget shortfalls constrained SIIPE effectiveness and sustainability.
claims.limitations: WFP notes gender analysis was constrained by missing disaggregated data and some benefits faded after payouts ended.

search_audit.query: Ethiopia Afar Somali Oromia climate displacement child drought flood named regional vulnerability report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF–IDMC identifies flood and drought displacement and service disruption in Afar, Somali and Oromia; IDMC adds Doolo Zone, Gafow, Koracle and Warder field findings.

search_audit.query: Ethiopia pastoral conflict drought water pasture Somali Afar Oromia local study
search_audit.outcome: The eastern Ethiopia study reports drought-linked water and pasture scarcity among respondents’ leading perceived conflict triggers, alongside political, property-rights and institutional factors; IDMC records recurrent conflict in the Somali Region displacement context.

search_audit.query: Ethiopia conflict insecurity reduces climate adaptation humanitarian delivery Somali Region displacement services
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF reports conflict-related disruption of livelihoods, education and health increases children’s exposure to climate shocks; IDMC says intercommunal conflict took humanitarian priority while aid shrank. No inspected source measures current insecurity effects on adaptation-project delivery.

search_audit.query: Ethiopia Somali pastoral drought adaptation resilience livestock insurance evaluation outcomes WFP
search_audit.outcome: WFP’s SIIPE evaluation summary reports food-security and financial-engagement gains but mixed livelihood effects and sustainability constraints; UNICEF recommends stronger inclusive services, child protection and displacement-sensitive planning.

gaps: The UNICEF–IDMC counts are historical estimates of displacement events rather than unique children; further research on Ethiopia-specific climate-conflict dynamics and long-term child outcomes is needed.
IDMC’s 2019 interview sample was purposive and camp-based, not representative; evidence is dated and does not establish current humanitarian conditions.
The 2013–2014 pastoral-conflict study is localized and perception-based; it does not isolate drought’s causal contribution or establish current institutional capacity.

WFP’s public evaluation landing-page summary was accessible, but its linked report PDF was blocked by a bot-verification challenge; no detailed result tables or full evaluation methods were inspected.
